task: Replace leaderboard population scans in accepted-race percentile rewards

requirements.RRI01: Exact percentile rewards with work independent of board population.
requirements.RRI02: Preserve ties, submitted-time comparisons, visibility, receipts, wallet atomicity and historical results.
requirements.RRI03: Validate transactional projection, migration and concurrency on actual PostgreSQL and SQLite.
requirements.R01: Preserve concurrent workspace work and original scoring contracts.
requirements.Q01: Retain commands, original reproduction, measured evidence and rollout limitations.

implementation.choice: Sparse database-maintained Fenwick prefix counters for race and independent flying-lap PBs.
implementation.reason: The reward needs exact counts below a tick and the exact eligible population, not the underlying player rows. A prefix index replaces repeated population scans with a small bounded set of primary-key lookups and updates only when a contributing PB or its eligibility changes.
implementation.query_bound: One SELECT per metric, at most 32 indexed counter rows including the population root, independent of the number of accounts or drivers. No player/PB COUNT, no range scan over all distinct times and no request-time rebuild.
implementation.domain: All positive PostgreSQL INTEGER tick values (1..2147483647), including historical boards, share a 2147483648 root. Counts use BIGINT. Existing valid results beyond today's 216000-tick verifier cap remain representable.
implementation.writes: PB insertion/removal updates at most 32 nodes. PB corrections/improvements cancel nodes common to the old/new paths, including the population root. Tied source changes and non-PB repeat attempts do not rewrite prefix counters. Empty nodes remain reusable; growth is tied to observed tick paths rather than attempts or player identities.
implementation.consistency: PostgreSQL and SQLite triggers maintain the projection in the same transaction as PB inserts, corrections, deletes and account disabled/deleted/artificial changes. Visibility updates count the old field before other triggers can retire PBs. PostgreSQL retains Player -> Board -> counter lock order. Counters cannot become negative, and missing negative-delta nodes fail the PostgreSQL transaction.
implementation.reward_policy: Use strictly faster times so equal times retain equal tiers. Compare integer rank*100 with population*tier to avoid floating point boundary ambiguity. Continue evaluating the actual submitted race/lap time, including slower repeats. Skip percentile queries after the existing 500-Coin maximum milestone. Existing CoinReward and wallet transaction fences remain.
implementation.migration: 0045_reward_rank_index backfills eligible existing race/lap PBs once, grouping equal times before expanding prefix paths. PostgreSQL write-locks the source tables for a consistent seed. It does not replay rewards or alter balances, receipts, results or manifests.
implementation.rollout: Back up and quiesce writers, apply the current complete migration chain including 0045, then start matching API/worker artifacts. The source-table lock and backfill require a measured rollout window on large databases. No live migration or deployment was performed.
alternatives: Cached/stale histogram or newspaper percentile thresholds were rejected for authoritative rewards: they can change who earns a tier.
SUM over all exact-time frequency rows removes player joins but still scans the time population; it is not a bounded prefix lookup.

Coarse buckets alone would approximate reward boundaries. An exact bucket-plus-detail design trades fewer counter writes for wider bounded reads; the prefix index favors frequent exact reward reads and reuses one narrow key lookup shape.
An in-memory tree or new external ranking service adds synchronization/recovery work and cannot share the existing atomic reward transaction.
implementation.tradeoffs: The index adds persisted counter rows and PB-update work. Common-ancestor cancellation and the maximum-tier fast path reduce it. Existing hot Board/track/queue contention is a separate concern; this change alone is not a million-DAU capacity certification.

cases: migration backfill/downgrade preserves existing result identities
counter populations above signed INTEGER range
population-root physical identity unchanged by improvements
end-to-end acceptance has zero population scans
maximum-tier fast path retains ordinary rewards
existing coin idempotency, spending, retention and account erasure
validation.original_reproduction: The saved original award function fails the unchanged end-to-end no-scan assertion and emits four PB/player population COUNT statements. Current implementation passes. Only the function is substituted in-process against disposable SQLite; no shared runtime file is reverted.
validation.postgres: Actual PostgreSQL tests use generated isolated schemas in the documented bmt-backend-test fixture. Windows port forwarding remained unreachable even outside the sandbox; the final runner uses a disposable cached backend image sharing only that fixture's network namespace, with current backend source mounted read-only. Credentials are read from the documented test env file without printing or saving them.
validation.benchmark: postgres-benchmark.json: 12 alternating warm samples at 1000, 10000 and 100000 synthetic drivers, using actual migration/backfill and rank query code. Old four-count medians 4.849/22.967/143.498 ms; new two-query medians 1.533/2.024/1.779 ms. The 100000-driver query used an Index Scan returning 10 rows with 28 shared buffer hits. PB-update EXPLAIN includes its actual trigger. This excludes HTTP, upload and complete verification and is not production throughput.
initial_corrections: The first test oracle probed MAX_INTEGER+1 after changing a synthetic PB to MAX_INTEGER; restrict probes to the supported candidate domain.
A lap-source repair assertion read an ORM object cached before a SQL trigger updated it; expire the fixture identity map before checking the database. No runtime assertion or policy changed.
Initial Windows PostgreSQL tests timed out on the forwarded fixture port. Retain those setup errors separately from the successful container-local tests.

Concurrent queue/Studio work briefly introduced migration-head naming conflicts. Preserve their files and keep reward migration 0045 based on 0044; the current queue migration merges the independent branches. No unrelated source was reverted.
